title: Chen Nian's Resolve
next_chapter_hook: The words their father spoke on his deathbed—"The turtle shell is only one of the keys"—echoed in Chen Nian's mind. Where, then, was the other relic hidden?

text.content: The Mortal Realm, the old Chen family residence. Night fell like ink, rain pouring down in torrents. Chen Nian sat alone in the study, her fingertips gently caressing a blood-stained Jade Slip, her expression calm as still water. Three days ago, her most trusted maid, Yunque, had vanished. Today, she had nailed the woman to the pillar of the Chen family ancestral hall. Blood dripped down the cracks in the Jade Slip, a shocking sight. She slowly raised her head, and lightning flashed outside the window, illuminating the rare, cold severity on her beautiful face. "Yunque, I treated you like a sister, yet you sold my whereabouts to the Holy Sect." Her voice was soft, yet each word cut like a blade. "The Chen family never betrays its own."

dialogue.content: "Young miss... young miss, spare my life! It was the Holy Sect people who forced me—they took my family hostage..." Yunque's voice had faded to a dying whisper.

text.content: Chen Nian closed her eyes, her lashes trembling slightly. She recalled how Yunque had taken a blade for her in childhood, the years they had fought side by side. Yet the next moment, she opened her eyes, leaving only cold emptiness within. She raised her hand, and a precise burst of Spiritual Energy sealed Yunque's meridians—not fatal, but preventing any further pleas. "You're right, they took your family." Chen Nian's voice was terrifyingly calm. "So I will avenge you, then send you to meet them."

Just then, the transmission Jade Talisman at Chen Nian's waist suddenly glowed. Frowning slightly, she extended her divine sense, and a familiar face appeared in her consciousness—her good-for-nothing brother, Chen Ji. In the projection, Chen Ji's expression was grave: "Niannian, has anything unusual happened in the Mortal Realm? Su Qingyao sent word that the Holy Sect is making big moves. I suspect their target is you." A faint smile curved Chen Nian's lips, yet carried a hint of bitterness: "Brother, your information is quite timely. Unfortunately, you're too late—the traitor has already been dealt with."

dialogue.content: "Dealt with?" The frowning Chen Ji on the other end of the transmission asked, "Yunque?"

"Mmm." Chen Nian responded softly, her gaze falling on the lifeless body pinned to the ancestral hall pillar. "Someone from the Holy Sect contacted her three days ago, threatening her parents' lives. She couldn't hold out."

choice.prompt: Upon learning Yunque was dead, Chen Ji fell silent for a moment before speaking.

choices.description: Chen Ji chose to trust his sister's judgment, allowing Chen Nian full authority over Mortal Realm affairs
choices.visible_cost: Unable to control the Mortal Realm situation
choices.visible_reward: Chen Nian gains freedom of action, the Chen family disciples unite as one
choices.risk_hint: If Chen Nian faces danger, an important asset will be lost

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's voice came through the transmission, carrying traces of exhaustion: "Alright. I trust you." After a pause, he added, "The Mortal Realm's affairs, you handle. But Niannian, if things become untenable, you must retreat. You're the only sister I have."

text.content: Chen Nian's eyes grew hot, but she forced herself to hold back. Taking a deep breath, her voice returned to its usual cold composure: "Brother, don't worry. Go do what you need to do. I won't drag you down in the celestial chess game. But as for the Mortal Realm—" She glanced at the十余名陈家子弟 kneeling outside the ancestral hall, a sharp gleam flickering in her eyes. "With me here, no one can touch the Chen family's roots."

The other end of the transmission fell silent for a moment, then Chen Ji's low laughter came through: "Good. Then I'll be up in the Heavenly Realm, tearing the Holy Sect's old lair apart for you." Hearing this, a genuine smile finally appeared on Chen Nian's face: "Then I'll be watching, waiting to see my brother display his divine might."

Just as Chen Ji was about to disconnect the transmission, Chen Nian suddenly spoke: "Brother, wait." Her voice trembled slightly, as if hesitating over something. Chen Ji refocused his attention: "What is it?" Chen Nian bit her lip and said quietly: "Before our father died, besides the turtle shell... he left me one more thing. He said it was the last road left for the Chen family." The transmission fell into sudden silence.

choices.description: Chen Ji intends to temporarily set aside Heavenly Realm arrangements and descend personally to support Chen Nian
choices.visible_cost: Disrupting Heavenly Realm plans, potentially missing crucial timing
choices.visible_reward: Brother and sister united can ensure Mortal Realm safety
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Realm allies may fall into danger as a result

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's gaze sharpened abruptly: "Where are you? I'm coming down right now." Yet Chen Nian shook her head: "Brother, no need. I can handle this."

text.content: Chen Ji frowned tightly, clearly uneasy. But Chen Nian spoke first: "Brother, don't forget your identity. How can the holder of the Tianji Record spare attention for a mess in the Mortal Realm? The Holy Sect is watching you, and those old foxes in the Heavenly Realm are watching too. If you return now, you'll fall right into their trap." Her tone turned uncharacteristically stern. "I am the Chen family's legitimate daughter. Mortal Realm affairs should be my burden to bear."

choices.description: Chen Ji demanded more clues from Chen Nian, intending to follow the trail to uncover the mastermind behind
choices.visible_cost: May expose one's attention to the mortal realm
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence and expose the Holy Sect's hidden agents in the mortal realm
choices.risk_hint: The interrogation process may alert the Holy Sect

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's gaze turned cold: "Who is behind Yunque? Which branch of the Holy Sect? Were there any survivors?" Chen Nian paused briefly, then understood her brother's meaning. After a moment of contemplation: "One escaped. Currently being pursued."

text.content: Chen Ji nodded: "Interrogate them and keep me updated. The Holy Sect has been maneuvering in the mortal realm for years - they wouldn't have sent only minor operatives. I want to see exactly which powerful force dares to reach out toward the Chen family." Chen Nian drew a deep breath, a fierce determination flashing in her eyes: "Understood. I'll dispatch my people right away."

The communication link trembled, and Chen Nian suddenly recollected something: "By the way, Brother. The turtle shell was merely one of Father's final possessions." Chen Ji froze: "What do you mean?" Chen Nian's voice dropped: "Before he died, Father entrusted me with a chest. He said, someday you would need it. But that chest... I've never managed to open it."

The communication link fell into an extended silence, so long that Chen Nian thought her brother had left. Thunder rumbled, the rain grew more violent, pattering densely against the ancestral hall's eaves. Finally, Chen Ji's voice returned, carrying an unprecedented gravity: "What else did Father say?" Chen Nian shook her head: "Nothing. But he left a key behind—one that can only be activated by our Chen bloodline." She paused, adding, "Brother, there's an inscription on the chest that I've never been able to decipher."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian slowly closed her eyes, as if recalling those ancient characters carved on the chest: "'When heavenly secrets remain incomplete, the chest opens a path of life.' Brother, what was Father trying to say? Does the Tianji Record... have something to do with this chest?" This time, the communication link fell into complete silence.

text.content: Outside the ancestral hall, the kneeling Chen family descendants maintained their postures, allowing the rain to drench them. They were the last remnants of the Chen bloodline—almost all of the parental generation had perished in that catastrophe twenty years ago, leaving only Chen Nian and Chen Ji as orphans. Now with Yunque's betrayal, they realized the Chen family had been thoroughly infiltrated. Had Chen Nian not acted decisively, the consequences would have been unthinkable.

Chen Nian walked to the entrance of the ancestral hall, her gaze sweeping across those loyal faces. In the curtain of rain, her voice was cold and resolute: "Rise. From today, the Chen descendants shall disperse and hide, secretly monitoring all suspicious individuals in the city. The person behind Yunque—I will drag them out myself." She turned, casting a final glance at the corpse on the pillar, complex emotions flickering in her eyes: "As for Yunque... sentenced for the crime of betraying the clan, to be cremated and scattered, denied entry to the ancestral burial ground."

dialogue.content: "One more thing—" Chen Nian's voice suddenly softened, carrying a rare tenderness, "Brother, no matter what's inside that chest, you must remember one thing." From the communication link came a soft grunt: "Speak." Chen Nian gazed at the ancestral tablets in the hall, a faint smile curling her lips: "No matter how many secrets the Chen family holds, one thing will never change—we are blood-related. Even if the heavens fall, I will stand by your side."

text.content: The communication link fell into a long silence. When Chen Ji spoke again, his voice had returned to its usual composure, yet beneath that composure seemed to surge some hidden undercurrent: "I understand. We'll address the chest matter once I have free hands here. Take care of yourself." Chen Nian nodded: "You too. Brother—" She hesitated, then finally said it, "Don't die out there. You promised Father you would take care of me for a lifetime." The communication abruptly cut off.

Chen Nian stood alone in the center of the ancestral hall, surrounded by the tablets of ancestors and the honor the Chen family had earned through generations of blood and sacrifice. The rain gradually subsided, clouds parting to reveal a bright, pristine moon. Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, illuminating the resolute determination on her beautiful face. She turned and walked toward the depths of the hall, where there was a secret chamber, and within it sat an ancient bronze chest. The chest was covered in intricate symbols, and at its center赫然 stood the mark of the Tianji Record—a half-open eye.

choice.prompt: Chen Nian stood in the secret chamber, the bronze chest emanating a faint, eerie glow.

choices.description: Forcefully activate the chest using Chen bloodline, regardless of any consequences
choices.visible_cost: May trigger unknown dangers or mechanisms
choices.visible_reward: Gain advance knowledge of the chest's contents and seize the initiative
choices.risk_hint: Father's warning surely carries deep meaning; forceful activation may prove counterproductive

text.content: Chen Nian took a deep breath, bit through her fingertip, and let a drop of blood fall onto the chest's lid. The bronze chest immediately shuddered violently, symbols flashing madly. However, just then, an aged voice rang in her mind: "Chen descendant, the time has not yet come." The symbols on the chest abruptly dimmed, falling silent. Chen Nian stumbled backward, her face pale—the voice was identical to her father's voice in his final moments.

She looked down at the wound on her fingertip; the blood droplet had already clotted, yet an inexplicable chill rose from the depths of her heart. Father's words echoed in her mind: "When heavenly secrets remain incomplete, the chest opens a path of life." Could "heavenly secrets incomplete" refer to the Tianji Record not yet being complete? Or could it be that her brother's Tianji Record shares some connection with this chest?

choices.description: Following her father's dying instructions, she kept the box and planned to wait until Chen Ji finished his affairs in the Heavenly Realm before making any decisions.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily losing the opportunity to make advance arrangements.
choices.visible_reward: To avoid triggering unknown risks, waiting until the siblings could act together before opening it.
choices.risk_hint: During this period, if anything unexpected happened, the box might be taken by others.

text.content: Chen Nian withdrew her hand, her gaze lingering on the box for a moment before she turned and left the secret chamber. She resealed the mechanisms of the chamber and arranged three layers of barriers outside. Since this box was connected to the Tianji Record, it was not something she could handle alone. Her brother held the Tianji Record Fragment in his hands, and perhaps only when he gathered more fragments and understood more of the truth would this box truly open.

The moment she stepped out of the secret chamber, Chen Nian suddenly felt an inexplicable lightness. She raised her head toward the horizon, where the bright moon hung high, its clear radiance spilling down. Chen Ji was making his moves in the Heavenly Realm, while she guarded the mortal world. The brother and sister each performed their own duties, yet their blood bond remained unbreakable. "Brother, don't worry." She murmured softly, "No matter how the chaos transforms this world, the Chen family... will not fall."

She turned toward the ancestral hall's entrance, where the Chen family disciples had already reformed their ranks, waiting. Chen Nian's gaze swept across their faces, finally landing on the one-armed young man at the very front—he was Chen Tie's distant cousin, who had lost his left arm in that catastrophe years ago but remained steadfastly loyal. "Brother Tie," she spoke, her voice cold yet carrying unmistakable authority, "from today onward, you will serve as the commander of the Chen family's Shadow Guard. Yun Que's entire network of connections, I want to take full control of. Since the Holy Sect dares to move against the Chen family, don't blame me for being merciless."

The one-armed young man knelt on one knee, his voice hoarse yet firm: "Your subordinate obeys!" Chen Nian gave a slight nod, cast one final glance toward the direction of the secret chamber deep within the ancestral hall, then stepped into the night. Moonlight stretched her silhouette long and long, like a path leading into the unknown. She didn't know what secrets the box held, nor how deep her father's布局 extended. But one thing she was certain of—no matter what lay ahead, she would guard this foundation for her brother until he returned victorious.

choices.text: Handing it over to her brother.
choices.description: Deciding to transfer the box along with all the clues to Chen Ji, letting him decide how to handle it.
choices.visible_cost: Losing the chance to control the secret alone.
choices.visible_reward: Gaining Chen Ji's complete trust, bringing the sibling relationship even closer.
choices.risk_hint: The box might be intercepted during the transfer.

text.content: Chen Nian drew a transmission jade talisman from her sleeve. After hesitating for a moment, she pressed it against the bronze box. This jade talisman was a relic left by the Chen family's ancestors, capable of transmitting objects across realms in a short time—the cost being the consumption of a large amount of the user's vital essence. But for her brother, she didn't care.

Just as she was about to activate the transmission formation, the runes on the box suddenly lit up, and a faint意念 transmitted into her mind: "My child... do not rush." Chen Nian's entire body trembled, nearly dropping the jade talisman. Father? That was father's voice! But father clearly had already... She jerked her head up, only to find the secret chamber empty, with not a single person in sight—only the bronze box glowing quietly under the moonlight.

At that moment, a black shadow descended from the sky, landing silently outside the secret chamber. Chen Nian instantly became alert, spiritual energy condensing in her hand as she coldly asked: "Who goes there?" The black shadow slowly turned, revealing a pale and familiar face—it was actually Mo Xiansheng, that mysterious Soul Guardian beside Chen Ji. "Chen family's girl," Mo Xiansheng's voice was aged and hoarse, "that box, you cannot touch it now."

Chen Nian's hand remained on the transmission jade talisman, her gaze sharp as a blade: "Mo Xiansheng? Why are you here?" Mo Xiansheng did not answer, only glancing at the bronze box, his clouded old eyes flickering with a complex light: "This old one received a commission from an old friend and has been waiting here for a long time. Girl, the things your father left behind are far more dangerous than you imagine." He paused, his voice dropping lower, "And also more important."

In the secret chamber, Chen Nian and Mo Xiansheng faced each other in confrontation. Moonlight filtered through the cracks, stretching their shadows into twisted shapes. Mo Xiansheng's gaze remained fixed on that bronze box, an indecipherable emotion appearing on his aged face—was that nostalgia, guilt, or... fear?

dialogue.content: "Mo Xiansheng," Chen Nian was the first to break the silence, her voice terrifyingly calm, "have you come to stop me?" Mo Xiansheng shook his head: "Not to stop, but to remind." He slowly walked toward the box, stopping at a distance of three feet, "Do you know what's inside this box?"

Chen Nian shook her head. Mo Xiansheng sighed: "That is... the other half of the Tianji Record." These words were like a thunderclap exploding in the secret chamber. Chen Nian's pupils constricted sharply, and she unconsciously gripped the transmission jade talisman in her hand tighter. The other half? Wasn't the Tianji Record only the one fragment in her brother's possession? How could there be another half? Just as she was about to ask, Mo Xiansheng had already continued speaking.

"Do you think the Tianji Record was merely obtained by luck by your brother?" Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a hint of mockery, "Chen family's girl, what the Chen family has guarded for generations has never been just one torn page. The true Tianji Record was divided into two halves from the very beginning—one in your brother's hands, to foresee the future; the other half..." He looked toward the bronze box, "sealed away, containing the truth of the past."

text.content: Chen Nian's heart suddenly accelerated. The past? The truth? She thought of her father's complex eyes before his death, remembered his words "When heavenly secrets are incomplete, the box opens a sliver of life," and suddenly understood. Heavenly secrets incomplete—her brother's Tianji Record was fragmentary, so he could only foresee three hours ahead. And what was sealed in this box was the key to completing the Tianji Record. Without it, her brother could never glimpse complete destiny. No wonder their father was so solemn before his death, no wonder he wanted to wait until "the time was ripe" before opening the box.

dialogue.content: "But—" Chen Nian's voice trembled slightly, "why did father leave something so important in the mortal world instead of giving it to brother?" Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment, as if weighing his words: "Because... the Heavenly Eye has been searching for the Tianji Record's whereabouts. The fact that your brother holds the fragment has already attracted its attention. If the two halves were placed together, once discovered, it would be an exterminating disaster."

text.content: Chen Nian instantly understood Mo Xiansheng's meaning. Father did this on purpose—he hid the other half of the Tianji Record in the mortal world, in the most hidden place of the Chen family ancestral home, to evade the Heavenly Dao's surveillance. While her brother's fragment could be sensed, after all, it was only a fragmentary corner, insufficient to expose the complete secret. But now... "So," Chen Nian's voice grew heavy, "what did father mean by 'the time is ripe'?" Mo Xiansheng's gaze fell on her, a flicker of approval appearing in his clouded old eyes: "You're very clever, girl. 'The time is ripe' refers to—" he paused, "when your brother gathers all the fragments of the Tianji Record."

dialogue.content: "Wait," Chen Nian敏锐ly caught the key information, "all fragments? Isn't the one in brother's hand the complete Tianji Record?" Mo Xiansheng shook his head: "Of course not. The Tianji Record has seven pages; your brother now has only one. The remaining six pages are scattered across the world—some in sect secret vaults, some deep within forbidden grounds, and some... in the Holy Sect's hands."

text.content: Chen Nian drew a sharp breath. She had always believed her brother was the luckiest person in the world, able to obtain the legendary Tianji Record. But now it seemed that was merely the beginning of a much larger chess game. Father, Mo Xiansheng, even the Tianji Record itself... everyone was arranging pieces. And she and her brother were merely the two most important chess pieces on the board. Outside the window, the east had begun to glow with the pale light of dawn. Chen Nian took a deep breath and made her decision.

"Mo Xiansheng," she raised her head, her gaze burning with intensity, "I don't care about any chess games or heavenly dao. The Chen family has never accepted fate." She tucked the Transmission Jade Talisman back into her sleeve, turning to look at the bronze box, "Since the time hasn't come yet, I'll guard this thing well for my brother. When he needs it, I will personally place it in his hands." Hearing this, a hint of moisture actually flickered in Mo Xiansheng's turbid old eyes: "Good... good child. If your father had known this in the underworld, he would surely be gratified."

With that, Mo Xiansheng's figure began to turn transparent, as if he would dissipate in this dawn at any moment. Before disappearing, he suddenly spoke: "Girl, remember one thing—your brother is more lonely than you can imagine." His voice drifted and wavered, as if coming from very far away, "The price of the Tianji Record isn't just Heavenly Fate Value. Each time it's used, his bonds with this world fade a little more. When you see him again... perhaps, he will no longer be the person he once was." As the words fell, Mo Xiansheng's figure completely vanished in the morning light. Only Chen Nian remained in the secret chamber, along with the bronze box emanating a faint, eerie glow.

Chen Nian stood in place, speechless for a long while. Loneliness, bonds, fate... these words echoed repeatedly in her mind. She suddenly recalled the transmission from her brother just now, recalled his words 'The matters of the mortal realm, you handle,' recalled his brief silence when hearing of Yun Que's betrayal. At that moment, she thought her brother was simply worried. But thinking about it now, perhaps what he was silent about wasn't just because of Yun Que's betrayal—and it was because he had long foreseen this moment. Brother... he had known someone would betray him all along, right?

Chen Nian closed her eyes, forcing herself to calm down. She was the Chen family's legitimate daughter, her brother's sister, and an indispensable piece in this game of chess. Since fate had her guard the mortal realm, she would do what she was meant to do. Cleansing the household, purging internal traitors, protecting the Chen family's foundations... and guarding that secret that even her brother didn't know about. She took one last look at the bronze box and walked out of the secret chamber. Morning light fell, illuminating the resolute determination on her beautiful face. No matter how many storms raged in the heavenly realm, the foundations of the mortal realm must not waver.

Three days later. A piece of news spread like wildfire across the mortal realm—Miss Chen had purged internal traitors with thunderous methods, executing over a dozen betrayers, and in one swift move destroyed the largest hidden stronghold the Holy Sect had established in the mortal realm. The Chen family, once regarded as 'weak and easily bullied,' had overnight displayed a foundation that inspired dread in all. At the same time, a transmission silently crossed the boundary, entering a certain secret location in the heavenly realm. In the transmission, there was only a short sentence: 'Brother, the mortal realm is settled, don't worry. What you need is in the box, I will present it to you personally when you return. — Nian.'
